article.name: ByteChef
article.summary: ByteChef combines workflow-integrated chat-memory backends with a document knowledge base. The reviewed knowledge-base path loads, chunks, embeds and retrieves documents through a shared pgvector vector store, with metadata filters and knowledge-base scoping. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark measurement.

who_what.text: The official README presents ByteChef as an open-source AI-agent and workflow automation platform maintained by the ByteChef team. It lists eight chat-memory backends and a built-in knowledge-base/vector-store path; this review focuses on the latter.

architecture.text: The knowledge-base component registers load, search, update, and delete actions plus vector-store and search cluster elements for agent workflows. It wires these through platform knowledge-base services and a shared Spring AI vector store.
A knowledge-base record carries a name, description, environment, tags, optimistic version, and chunk settings. The source defaults are maxChunkSize 1024, minChunkSizeChars 100, and overlap 200.

Document rows carry a file-storage entry, knowledge-base ID, size, tags, status, created/modified actor and timestamps, and version. Chunk rows link to a document and vector-store ID, with file content; retrieval text, metadata, and score are transient fields.

The adapter adds knowledge-base, document, chunk, environment, and tag metadata around vector records. README setup instructions say the internal knowledge base requires PostgreSQL with pgvector and that the shared embedding model is globally configured.

behavior.text: Load reads documents through a selected reader and configured splitter/enricher transformers, then sends transformed records through the shared vector-store adapter. The load action chooses the target knowledge-base ID.

Update selects a document or chunk to replace, optionally using metadata filters. The adapter removes old chunk rows and matching vector entries before loading replacements; document-level update can inherit existing metadata and overlay new values.

Delete is available by metadata filter. The wrapper adds the selected knowledge-base ID condition to metadata-filter deletions; complete physical erasure through backups and external storage retention was not inspected.

Search supports vector similarity for nonblank queries and filter-only retrieval when a query is empty but tags or metadata filters are present. Top-K defaults to 10, threshold to 0.0, tag filters are OR-ed, and the selected knowledge-base predicate is AND-ed with other filters.

metrics.evidence: The source shows semantic vector retrieval and a filter-only route, but no answer-quality or abstention probes were run.
Source has document/chunk replacement operations and version fields; no correction adjudication or stale-value workload was run.
Metadata-filter deletion exists and is KB-scoped in the wrapper; no post-delete leak check or backup-erasure audit was performed.
Query filters bind vector retrieval to a KB ID in source; no cross-tenant or cross-KB isolation experiment was run.
Document/chunk IDs, file references, metadata, and similarity scores are inspectable; no generated-answer support or citation adjudication was conducted.

metrics.metric: Latency, write-to-recall delay, tokens/cost, and storage
metrics.evidence: Source exposes chunking, top-K, threshold, and byte-accounting controls, but no system or benchmark measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded read-only inspection of the official README, knowledge-base component actions, vector-store wrapper and adapter, and domain models at the verified head. It does not establish deployed configuration, relevance quality, or runtime reliability.

The wrapper demonstrates query-level KB scoping for vector similarity search and metadata-filter deletion. It does not alone establish tenant authorization or isolation across every vector-store access path.

The inspected provenance fields link stored documents and chunks to files, actors, times, versions, and retrieval metadata; they do not prove claim correctness, end-to-end answer citations, or erasure from backups/replicas.

benchmark.note: No ByteChef runtime, benchmark workload, or tests were run. Source observations are not measured results.
